sentences.text: The genus Lamarqueavis was named in 2010 by Agnolin, with the type species L. australis based on a partial right coracoid fossil found in the Allen Formation of Argentina.
The holotype specimen MML 207 is an incomplete right coracoid that preserves the proximal articular surfaces and is housed in the Municipal Museum of Lamarque.
Despite being fragmentary, the presence of a triradiate concavity in the coracoid distinguishes Lamarqueavis from Enantiornithes and links it to basal Neornithes.
The generic name Lamarqueavis is derived from Lamarque, a locality near the fossil site, and avis, the Latin word for 'bird'.
Lamarqueavis lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Lamarqueavis lived during the Late Cretaceous period and its fossils have been found in Argentina, Canada, and the United States.

The discovery of Lamarqueavis in the Allen Formation, which shows signs of tidal action, supports the hypothesis that early Neornithes lived in coastal environments while Enantiornithes inhabited continental areas.
